title: Vibhishana's crossing
hook: the enemy's brother asks to be let in; the camp argues; Rama makes a vow

segments.voice: Yesterday: Vibhishana's crossing began. He told Ravana the truth, was called a disgrace, and your line, I've come for refuge, as he crossed the sea. Did you wait a breath before answering something hard? A new week begins, with Vibhishana hanging in the sky over Rama's camp. Day six hundred thirty-eight.

A war camp on a beach, the eve of battle. A figure appears in the sky above it, with four armed companions, and calls down: I'm the enemy king's brother, please let me in. Sugriva, king of the monkeys, doesn't hesitate. He goes straight to Rama and says: this is a trick. He's a rakshasa, he's Ravana's own brother, and he'll strike when we're not looking. Kill him, or send him away. The whole camp starts arguing.
screen: `A FIGURE IN THE SKY.` → `THIS IS A TRICK.` → `THE CAMP ARGUES.`

segments.voice: Rama asks his council, and Valmiki lets every voice speak. Angada says test him first. Others say send a spy, or question him closely. Jambavan is suspicious of the timing. Then Hanuman speaks, and he's the one who has actually been inside Lanka. He came openly, Hanuman says, not in disguise. I've watched his face, and I see no deceit in it. He knows Ravana's wrongs and he's seen your strength. Accept him. Then Rama gives his answer. I can't turn away someone who comes as a friend, he says, even if he has faults. Then he says something larger. Anyone who comes to me even once and says, I am yours, I give safety from every being. That is my vow. Sugriva still pushes back. Rama goes further. Even if it were Ravana himself, he says, bring him in. In the Sri Vaishnava tradition of South India, this verse is treasured as a teaching on sharanagati, taking refuge, or surrender: the one who turns to God even once, sincerely, is held. Others read it more plainly, as the code of a good king toward someone asking for protection. And then Rama does something practical and startling. He has Vibhishana come down, sends for sea water, and pours it over his head, consecrating him king of Lanka, right there on the beach, before a single battle has been fought.
screen: `EVERY VOICE IN THE COUNCIL.` · `HANUMAN: I SEE NO DECEIT.` · `ANYONE WHO SAYS I AM YOURS.` · `KING OF LANKA, ON THE BEACH.` · then, large: `EVEN IF IT WERE RAVANA HIMSELF.`

segments.voice: Sit comfortably and let the breath come and go. Bring to mind someone who has come to you, once, asking for help or a second chance, someone you weren't sure you could trust. Picture them at the edge of your camp. You don't have to decide anything about them. Just let the door in your chest open by one inch. Breathe in, and notice the caution. Breathe out, and notice the welcome. Let both be there. The bell holds the time.
Vibhishana's crossing. The enemy's brother asks for refuge, the camp argues, and Rama vows safety to anyone who comes even once and says, I am yours.
Your line: even if it were Ravana. Today, when someone asks to be let in, hear them out before the camp decides. Day six hundred thirty-eight.

howItsDone: In the Sri Vaishnava tradition the Vibhishana episode is taught as the model of śaraṇāgati, taking refuge, and Rama's vow in Yuddha Kanda 18 is recited and commented on as a central verse.

fork.setup: you're Rama. your closest ally says the enemy's brother is a spy. Hanuman says his face shows no deceit. what do you do?
options: send him away to be safe.
test him for a few days first.
take him in: anyone who comes asking for refuge is safe with you.
fork.reveal: Rama vows safety to anyone who comes even once and says I am yours, and crowns Vibhishana on the beach.

original.note: Sanskrit śaraṇāgati: coming for refuge, from śaraṇa, refuge or shelter, and āgati, arrival; a key word in Sri Vaishnava teaching.

trapdoor: what you thought: Rama took Vibhishana in because he was useful.
what it means: Rama makes a vow: anyone who comes even once and says I am yours is given safety, even Ravana.
what a scholar hears: Sri Vaishnava teachers treat this verse (sakṛd eva prapannāya…) as one of the great verses on surrender to God.
